title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a notational digression. It belongs to the long section of the 'Longue Marche' continuation that studies profinite groups M_{ρ,σ}. These are built from the modular group: ρ and σ appear to be the standard torsion elements of SL(2,Z), of orders 6 and 4 with ρ^3 = σ^2 = -1, and μ_ρ seems to be the central subgroup {±1}. The groups are extensions of an 'extended' Galois group Γ_Q^~ by profinite completions of (subgroups of) SL(2,Z).

On the previous page Grothendieck had:
- set up an exact sequence 1 → μ → M^~_{ρ,σ}(-J) → Γ^~_{ρ,σ} → 1;
- found partial sections over Γ^~_{ρ,σ};
- identified index-2 and index-4 subgroups as kernels of a sign character ε_2.

Here he steps back and asks which groups deserve the simplest notation: M_{ρ,σ} or the quotients M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ =: M^~_{ρ,σ}. He judges the quotients the most interesting. His reason is that they relate to the 'universal group' M = N^~_{1,1}, written with a Gothic 𝔖 symbol and a profinite hat. This is the extension of Γ_Q^~ by SL(2,Z)^, i.e. the (extended) arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{1,1} of elliptic curves.

The obstacle is that the tilde is already used in a different sense, in Γ_Q^~, M_{0,3}^~, etc., and the exponents ', '', ''', °, +, !, ♮ are all taken. He proposes replacing the tilde of Γ_Q^~ by a superscript 'ét' (for 'étendu') or 'gén' (for 'généralisé'). He then postpones the whole question: the next page says to keep the current notations and revise them in a special later §.

The mathematical content is thus a single structural remark. The extended Galois group Γ_Q^~ is something that 'extends' or 'generalizes' Gal(Q̄/Q), which is the role later played by Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups. The various M_{ρ,σ} groups are viewed as pieces of the universal extension 1 → SL(2,Z)^ → N^~_{1,1} → Γ_Q^~ → 1.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is about notation.
The claim that the quotients by μ_ρ are 'the more interesting' is a judgement, not a result.

A quotient by the center μ_ρ = {±1} would more naturally sit over PSL(2,Z)^ than SL(2,Z)^. The text links it to an extension by SL(2,Z)^, which may reflect the stacky (generic ±1 automorphism) picture of M_{1,1}. As written, the precise relation between M^~_{ρ,σ} and N^~_{1,1} is not explained on this page.

ideas.what: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} as an extension of an (extended) absolute Galois group by the profinite completion of SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}) / profinite SL(2,Z) extension; arithmetic of the Teichmüller tower in genus 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Nakamura, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1}); La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Γ_Q^~ as an 'étendu/généralisé' Galois group, to be denoted Γ_Q^ét or Γ_Q^gén
ideas.modern_name: Enlarged/combinatorial Galois group, cf. Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (Drinfeld 1990), or Galois group extended by complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara for GT^; Grothendieck's idea of a combinatorial Teichmüller group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the idea; the 'étendu' terminology seems unpublished

ideas.what: Notational conflict between tilde as 'quotient by μ_ρ' and tilde as 'extended'

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly glosses the tilde in Γ_Q^~ as 'étendu' or 'généralisé'. This is documentary evidence that his Γ_Q^~ was conceived as an enlargement of Gal(Q̄/Q), a GT-like object acting on the whole tower including N_{1,1}.
missed.quote: remplacer le ∼ des Π_Q^∼ par des lettres telles que Γ_Q^ét (suggérant "étendu") ou "généralisé"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for establishing what Grothendieck meant by his extended Galois group before Drinfeld's GT. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mainly notational housekeeping. The only point of interest is the explicit gloss of Γ_Q^~ as an 'extended/generalized' Galois group and the identification of the 'universal group' M = N^~_{1,1}, as an extension by SL(2,Z)^, as the organizing object. Both fit with what is known from the Esquisse and the Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'suggestions [?]' is more likely 'suggestives' or 'suggérées'; the handwriting is unclear.
'ressortissent [?] le groupe universel' should probably read 'qui ressortissent [au] groupe universel'. The symbol after it looks like a Gothic 𝔖_0 with a profinite hat, followed by '='.
Margin note: approximately 'plutôt, le groupe des points Ẑ-[entiers?] de ... ressortit...'. The reading 'Ẑ^×' is doubtful.
'les ∼ des Π_Q^∼' should be 'le ∼ des Γ_Q^∼' (Γ, not Π).
The list of exponents in the image includes ', '', ''', °, +, !, ♮, with a struck-out run of characters, followed by '(sont) déjà utilisés'.
The final line breaks off at 'ces di-' and continues on the next page as 'dilemmes notationnels'.
